definition: Urbanization means the growth of cities as more people move into them.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word urbanization. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know urbanization should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Decades of night-sky photographs trace the region's urbanization — the dark patches shrink in every frame as new grids of light switch on.
Growth says only that the town got bigger; urbanization says what it became — denser, taller, more urban, as newcomers arrived.
Sprawl is urbanization off its leash: not just cityward growth but growth flung outward, thin and unplanned, paving a county to house a suburb.

Development is building and business growth of any kind — a new mill town, a resort strip, a suburban office park — city or not. Urbanization is the narrower, demographic claim: people moving in and a place turning genuinely urban, its density and habits shifting cityward along with its buildings.

Industrialization is an economy's shift to factories and machine production. It often drives urbanization by pulling workers into town, but the two can part ways: a country can industrialize in scattered company towns, while urbanization names only the people, buildings, and city habits gathering together.

Anh's office, one surveyed in 1962 and one printed last spring.
On the old sheet, forty fishing villages dot the banks, each a cluster of a few hundred households ringed by rice terraces.
On the new sheet the villages have run together into one continuous city of two million, and the terraces survive only as street names.
Anh insists, are the least of it.
Urbanization is better read in her interview notes: grandchildren who commute by metro, buy breakfast from vendors, and have never planted anything.
